regime: Risk-on reversal. One day after the FOMC flush, NQ and ES reclaimed their ATR stops and flipped long on a tech-led, earnings-driven rally; gold held a haven bid, crude cooled.
summary: One day after the FOMC flush, the tape ripped it all back. NQ closed up 3.94 percent at 28,333.5, reclaimed its ATR stop, and flipped long. The driver was earnings, not macro: Microsoft jumped about 15 percent on blowout results and semis followed Samsung higher, so tech led the recovery. It happened despite a soft Q2 GDP print, 1.5 percent advance against roughly 2 percent expected and down from Q1, with the report's inflation gauges still elevated. ES flipped long too, up 1.90 percent, VIX collapsed 17 percent to 17.09, and gold held its haven bid up 0.88 percent while crude gave a little back at minus 0.85 percent.
psychology: Your bias resets every session. Anyone who stayed short after yesterday's hawkish close got squeezed today, because the tape does not owe the prior move a follow-through. The tell was mechanical: when price reclaims the ATR stop you were leaning against, that is the signal to stand down the old bias, not to double down on it. Trade the level in front of you, not the story you brought in from yesterday.
